source_caption_text:
He actually fooled everyone with this jolly ahh song 😭🙏

A federal jury found Lil Durk (Durk Banks) not guilty on all charges in his federal murder-for-hire trial after three days of deliberations.

His legal team secured the full acquittal primarily by undermining the credibility of the government’s key witnesses and highlighting gaps in the prosecution’s evidence. The prosecution relied heavily on three cooperating witnesses—including former associates and a former personal assistant—who testified that Durk ordered and funded the hit on rival rapper Quando Rondo in retaliation for the death of King Von. Durk’s lawyers, led by attorney Brian Steel, effectively attacked these witnesses as untrustworthy, arguing that they were fabricating claims about Durk’s involvement solely to receive reduced sentences for their own crimes. The defense instead pointed to Durk’s former assistant, Kavon Grant, as the true mastermind who acted independently and manipulated law enforcement into targeting the high-profile rapper.

Additionally, the prosecution’s physical evidence failed to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Durk personally orchestrated or directed the plot. While prosecutors introduced financial records showing travel bookings paid for by an associated credit card and text messages regarding the aftermath, jurors noted during post-trial interviews that the government failed to prove Durk exercised actual direct command over the individuals involved. The defense also successfully argued that his rap lyrics, public comments, and interviews—presented by the government as evidence of revenge motives—were merely artistic expression, internet posturing, and clickbait rather than proof of a criminal order. Unable to firmly link Durk as the organizer, the jury acquitted him on all counts.
